text:
maria: Posted an nsys + NVTX trace from a 90s synthetic load — seeing repeated 200-400ms spikes that look like compilation stalls between token batches. attaching link to perfetto slice: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234 :eyes:

kai: Can you paste the nvtx regions? do we have timestamps for the compile start/end?

maria: paste of the relevant snippet below:
```
NVTX: model::forward_start (0.0s)
NVTX: kernel_compile_start (12.3s)
NVTX: kernel_compile_end (12.7s)   # ~400ms
NVTX: model::forward_resume (12.7s)
```
spikes repeat ~every 3s for certain batch boundaries.

taylor: interesting — which kernels are compiling? deconv? einsum?

maria: top compiled kernels (from nsys summary): deconv_forward, ffn_gelu, rotary_unroll. deconv is most frequent. compile time distribution: [350, 420, 210, 380] ms samples.

samir: are these cold-starts from a new batch size/seq-len? or evictions from the kernel cache?

maria: looks correlated with KV cache misses too. when KV hit rate drops below ~85% we see more compile spikes. sequence lengths also jump from 32->512 at some requests.

kai: hypothesis: kernel selector chooses a new tiling variant for longer seqs, triggers Triton/XLA-like compile path and populates kernel cache. if cache is sharded per GPU we might be thrashing.

perf-bot: auto-report: compile-cache size=128 entries per-shard, eviction rate=0.12 evictions/s during trace. async-compile queue length peak=6.

taylor: that eviction rate is not huge but combined with different tilings it could cause churn. also async queue=6 means backpressure; request threads might block waiting for compile to finish.

maria: reproduction notes I used: 8xA100, batch mix with 1/3 long-seq requests, load ~1200 rps synthetic. command: 
```
nsys profile --output=trace.nsys --sample=cpu --trace=nvtx,cuda python run_load.py --mix long=0.33
```

samir: quick triage checklist:
- confirm kernel-cache shard affinity (are kernels reused across shards?)
- capture kernel cache keys for hot kernels (tile, dtype, seq-len)
- run a trace with KV cache pinned + no eviction (force keep) to see if spikes disappear

kai: also try pre-warming top-k kernels at startup: iterate over representative shapes and invoke compilation path with minimal inputs. That should amortize warmup. can run as a background job on pod init.

taylor: other mitigations: increase compile-cache size or enable cross-shard shared cache (if memory permits). or introduce a lightweight heuristic: if seq-len jumps are detected, queue precompile for likely kernels rather than on-demand in-request compile.

maria: did a quick experiment — warmed top 5 deconv variants at init, replayed the same load. still see residual 120-180ms spikes (smaller), appears to be remaining variants that weren't prewarmed.

samir: 120-180ms might be from constant JIT linking / kernel module load overhead. are we loading PTX binaries or doing full compile on device each time?

maria: nsys shows full JIT compile (device-side) for the big variants. PTX caching is enabled but seems index mismatch due to differing tile params.

kai: can we quantize/shrink variant space? e.g., prefer a small set of canonical tilings and fallback to slower kernels if not optimal but avoid compile cost. quality loss must be checked but it might be worth for latency SLOs.

taylor: also look at batching heuristics — if batching boundary causes seq-len mix changes, consider grouping similar seq-lens together to reduce variant churn. dynamic bucketing might help.

maria: Action items:
- (maria) run one trace with kernel-cache pinned and share nsys pkg (~today EOD)
- (kai) add NVTX regions around compile + cache lookup (so compile vs eviction is clear)
- (taylor) prototype prewarm job that covers top-10 observed variants across traces
- (samir) estimate memory cost for shared cache and run feasibility calc

samir: timeline for PRs?

kai: I'll open a small change to add NVTX annotations tomorrow morning. low-risk.

taylor: prewarm prototype — I can push a branch by mid-week to test.

maria: thanks all. leaving perfetto link and raw nsys bundle in the thread. tagging @kai @taylor for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
